title: Fake News on Social Media
text:
Many people read news on social media every day. Sometimes a post looks real, but the information is false. This is called fake news. Fake news can spread very fast because people share posts before they check them.

Before you share a story, you should read the whole article and check the source. Look for the name of the writer and the date of the post. If you are not sure, do not share it. Checking facts takes only a few minutes, but it can stop false information from spreading.

questions.text: Why can fake news spread very fast?
options: People share posts before they check them

questions.text: What should you look for before you share a story?
options: The name of the writer and the date

questions.text: What can we infer about the writer's opinion of sharing posts without checking them?
options: They think it can cause problems
They think it is always safe
They think it is a good way to make friends
They think news is always true

questions.text: Why does the writer say that checking facts can stop false information?
options: Because people will stop sharing unchecked posts
Because checking is faster than reading
Because phones do not show posts
Because the writer works for a newspaper

paragraph_translations: Muitas pessoas leem notícias nas redes sociais todos os dias. Às vezes, uma publicação parece real, mas a informação é falsa. Isso se chama fake news. As fake news podem se espalhar muito rápido porque as pessoas compartilham publicações antes de verificá-las.

Antes de compartilhar uma história, você deve ler o artigo inteiro e verificar a fonte. Procure o nome do autor e a data da publicação. Se você não tiver certeza, não compartilhe. Verificar os fatos leva apenas alguns minutos, mas pode impedir que informações falsas se espalhem.
